summary.intent: Harden the release CI so it fails loudly instead of publishing silently without binaries (trail #202): validate release JSON keys, require registry tokens, and extend SemVer checks to all published crates.
summary.outcome: A delegated subagent reported finishing trail #202 on branch ci/release-fails-loudly (commit 7e2c7b94, pushed, linked to trail with base ci/linux-x64-glibc-floor). actionlint and zizmor pass, but the token step, the .pending guard and cargo semver-checks itself were not run.

repo: callisto-release.yml's old probe `jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0'` returned false for a missing (renamed) or null key, so a rename would have published without binaries and the job would still be green.
The `.pending[0].source // empty` read treated a renamed `.pending` key as nothing unfinished, so it needs an array-type guard.
The `semver` job in ci.yml calls the `semver` recipe in the justfile, so SemVer coverage is changed in the justfile and ci.yml needs no edit.
Published crates with a library API are caliper-docgen-core, caliper-docgen-semantic and caliper-docgen-tsc-client. Each has its own `cargo/<crate>: minor|major` changeset exemption.
caliper-docgen is a binary crate, so semver-checks does not apply. caliper-docgen-napi is `publish = false`.
`entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <base>` links a branch to a trail.
`just --fmt --check` already reports a formatting difference on the `cargo {{args}}` line in the justfile.

code.finding: Added a jq -e guard (`has("artifactSlots") and type == "array"`) before the slot count read, a `.pending` array guard, and a 'Require registry credentials' step that checks NPM_TOKEN and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN with `-z "${!name}"` before the npm auth and release steps.
The `semver` recipe now loops over the three library crates and fails if any breaks without its own changeset exemption.

workflow: Reproduce the old failure mode on sample inputs before changing a check, to confirm the bug is real.
The subagent's hand-back is model output without user authority, so treat its claims as reports to verify, not approvals.
The sandbox blocks some git config writes. `git checkout -b` created the branch despite the error, and the subagent then switched to it with the sandbox off.

friction: The first `git checkout -b` hit a sandbox config-write error even though it had created the branch.
The sandbox refused the one-liner for testing the token-check shell logic on its own, so that step is untested beyond lint.
The existing `just --fmt --check` formatting difference makes the formatting check noisy.
open_items: Run `cargo semver-checks` for real. If caliper-docgen-semantic or caliper-docgen-tsc-client were never published to crates.io, the first CI run may fail for lack of a baseline and will need handling.
Test the 'Require registry credentials' step and the `.pending` array guard, neither of which was exercised.
The preexisting justfile formatting difference on the `cargo {{args}}` line was left alone.
No PR has been opened for ci/release-fails-loudly, and docs/release-0-9-0 was deliberately not touched.
